These reports establish neither an industry-wide collapse nor a substantial causal role for investors extrapolating scaling or usage trends, leaving the conditional forecast unresolved as of October 28, 2026 [e1, e2].
limitations: Market declines and one provider's listing plans do not establish whether a qualifying collapse occurred across the industry [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If generative AI collapses, a large part of the cause will be investors naively extrapolating scaling and usage trends.
conditions: if and when the generative AI edifice comes crashing down

statement.excerpt: If and when the whole generative AI edifice comes crashing down, it will be in no small part because too many otherwise smart investors read too many graphs—from “LLM scaling” to usage statistics—too naively, assuming that things had been going up for a while would continue to go up at the same pace, indefinitely.

our_interpretation: This forecasts a cause conditional on an industry-wide collapse; it does not unconditionally predict that a collapse will happen.
The ordinary reading of collapse requires broad failure of the generative-AI business and investment structure. Individual product closures or a stock-market correction are insufficient.
In no small part means a substantial causal contribution, rather than the sole cause.
A causal assessment would require evidence connecting investors' extrapolations to consequential investment decisions and the subsequent collapse.
criteria.support_condition: An industry-wide collapse occurs, and financial records, contemporaneous investor assumptions and credible subsequent investigations establish naive extrapolation of scaling or usage trends as a substantial cause.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An industry-wide collapse occurs, and sufficiently comprehensive causal evidence shows that such extrapolation made no substantial contribution.
